title: Logger requirements
idea: Scoping a logger system means fixing who writes logs, which levels exist, where lines go, and which promises the logger keeps while the app runs.
points: Application code logs a message at a level: DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR or FATAL.
Each logger has a threshold; messages below it are dropped cheaply.
Accepted messages become one record, formatted by and written to console, file, or both.
Logging must never crash the app or block it for long.

hero.title: Who uses the logger in v1

edges.caption: Code calls the logger with a level and a message. That is the main use case.
Only messages at or above the threshold go on. The rest cost almost nothing.
One accepted message becomes one line, sent to every configured output.
An operator raises or lowers a logger's level without a redeploy.
The new threshold applies to the very next call.
Sending logs to a central store and searching them is a separate system.

code.title: Levels and threshold
code.caption: The core rule as code: a message is written only if its level is at or above the threshold.

walk.text: Pick WARN as the threshold, the way an operator would in config.
Check every level against the threshold and print the decision.
Write the out-of-scope list down, so nobody builds it by accident.
Levels are declared from least to most severe.
Comparing positions answers "is this severe enough?" in one step.

pitfalls: Do not promise every line reaches disk if the process is killed; state the guarantee.
Never let a full disk or a broken file throw into business code.
Do not scope log search or shipping into the logger; that is another system.

quiz.q: An interviewer asks for logs searchable across 50 servers. What is the best v1 scoping answer?
options: Add a search index inside the Logger class
Write locally; a separate agent ships lines centrally
Make every Logger call POST to a search service
Refuse, because loggers never leave the machine
quiz.why: The logger's job is to write lines fast and safely. Collecting and searching them belongs to a separate pipeline, which keeps the logger small.

takeaway: Levels, a threshold, formatting and outputs; never crash or stall the app.
